name: Kerr parametric oscillator, half a stored photon
question: Does a Kerr parametric oscillator whose stored states hold less than one photon, swept through threshold with the same bias as the 27-photon oscillator, choose its state by the linear stage or by the balance of its two shallow wells?
assumptions: Frame rotating at half the pump frequency; hbar = 1; rates in units of the single-photon loss kappa.
The same sweep, hold and bias as the 27-photon oscillator; only the Kerr coefficient changes, from 0.02 to 1, so the stored states hold 0.48 photons instead of 27 and the two wells are shallow.
The bias is the one for which the Gaussian-stage law predicts a probability of 0.75.
A control of the linear-stage law: the exact probability is expected at the selection of the biased steady state, which the switching between the wells reaches during the sweep.

provenance.reference: few-photon Kerr parametric oscillators of Z. Wang et al., Phys. Rev. X 9, 021049 (2019) and N. E. Frattini et al., Phys. Rev. X 14, 031040 (2024)
